prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you give me a really strong wine that tastes like coffee and flowers, something totally weird I've never heard of, to go with a spicy curry?"

List A:
Wine 1: Pinot Noir, US, $65. Tasting note: "This unusual and attention-getting wine is full of spicy aromas and flavors, almost like a mulled wine, with cinnamon, clove and cardamom, plus a super-concentrated fruit core. The texture stays tangy despite the heavy spices, and the mouthfeel is very assertive and appetizing."
Wine 2: Cabernet Franc, US, $19. Tasting note: "Smelling this wine is like sticking your nose into a jar of turmeric, with added aromas of ground coffee bean and broad black fruit that shade in the background. While the turmeric note remains dominant on the palate, the wine would pair well with spicy curry dishes—especially considering its modest 12% alcohol."
Wine 3: Gewürztraminer, France, $20. Tasting note: "Typically spicy, this wine is all about intense perfumes. Very soft, ripe and rounded, it will be better as a sweet apéritif than with food."
Wine 4: Carmenère, Chile, $29. Tasting note: "Quite saucy and spicy upon first blush, with a heavy bouquet. Here's a wine that holds nothing back; it is compact, tight and hard on the palate, but it tastes meaty, big and generous, with plum and chocolate flavors. Finishes with heat, rusticity and peppery power. A brawny wine that shoots high but doesn't hit every target."
Wine 5: Pinot Noir, US, $44. Tasting note: "Perfumed in violet and rose, this wine is spicy in clove and nutmeg, a savory sneak that undermines the bright, high-toned cherry and berry in deliciously devious ways. Medium bodied with a tannic bite on the finish, it offers the best of both worlds in terms of elegance and oomph."

List B:
Wine 1: Gewürztraminer, US, $20. Tasting note: "Fresh and delicate with floral and citrus overtones, this wine has an elegant character. Its dry, spicy flavors are subtle and refreshing, giving the wine food pairing flexibility. Ideally, though, think of spicy cuisine like Indian, Thai or Indonesian."
Wine 2: Muscat, France, price unknown. Tasting note: "Attractive spicy wine with a lively, lightly spicy character. It is rich without being heavy, showing acidity while also having a smooth texture on the finish."
Wine 3: Bordeaux-style White Blend, France, $14. Tasting note: "Aromatic and floral, this wine has crisp fruitiness and lively acidity that support the delicious spicy character. Drink now."
Wine 4: Pinot Noir, US, $30. Tasting note: "This wine conveys cola, root beer, dried strawberry and graphite aromas, with an intriguing twist of curry spice. It's rich on the palate with decent weight, showing Indian spice, pepper, star anise and tart yet juicy cranberry."
Wine 5: Carignan, US, $38. Tasting note: "This savory, spicy wine is relatively light but offers a tasty combination of non-fruit flavors such as black pepper, beef broth and wood smoke. It's medium bodied, lightly tannic and quite complex for its moderate concentration."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
